overview: This 139-page file traces Japanese regulation of foreign aviation and U.S. diplomatic efforts to clarify and publish flight requirements. It covers routes, landing fields, permits, restricted areas, the Pangborn–Herndon investigation, jurisdiction over the South Manchuria Railway Zone, and translations of Japan’s 1921 Aviation Law and 1936 amendment.
interest: Diplomatic correspondence reveals contested railway-zone jurisdiction and how aviators’ violations shaped public guidance on Japanese flight rules.
